senses.obs_text: In the twenty verses G1380 is a mixture of opinion and question, the verb of what a person holds or is asked to hold. As a question to the hearer: what do you think (Mat 17:25, 18:12, 21:28, 22:17, 22:42, Joh 11:56), do you think (Mat 26:53, Luk 10:36, 12:51, 13:2, 13:4, Heb 10:29) and do not think (Joh 5:45), where Jesus asks or forbids an opinion. As a held view: the Gentiles who think they are heard for their many words (Mat 6:7), those who think the Scriptures give them life (Joh 5:39), those who kill thinking they serve God (Joh 16:2), Paul's judgment of the apostles' lot and of his own spirit (1Cor 4:9, 7:40), the parts of the body thought less honourable (1Cor 12:23), and the fear that Paul be thought foolish (2Cor 11:16). In all the word is a conviction or an estimate that is stated or asked for, and in several the verse tests it against a fact.
